intro: Professionals and everyday users convert kilometers per liter (km/L) to mpg (us) (MPG (US)) when working across metric and us_customary standards in comparing North American EPA window stickers against European WLTP and UK vehicle fuel consumption figures. One kilometers per liter equals 2.352146 mpg (us), while 1 miles per gallon (us) equals 0.425144 kilometers per liter. Whether you are verifying fuel economy specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many mpg (us) (MPG (US)) are in 1 kilometers per liter (km/L)?
faqs.answer: There are 2.35214583 mpg (us) (MPG (US)) in 1 kilometers per liter (km/L), which rounds to 2.3521 MPG (US) for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 miles per gallon (us) equals 0.425144 kilometers per liter.

faqs.question: How do I convert kilometers per liter to mpg (us) (km/L to MPG (US))?
faqs.answer: To convert kilometers per liter to mpg (us), use the formula: MPG (US) = km/L × 2.35214583. For example, converting 20 km/L gives 47.0429 MPG (US).

faqs.question: What is 20 kilometers per liter in mpg (us)?
faqs.answer: 20 kilometers per liter (km/L) equals exactly 47.0429 mpg (us) (MPG (US)) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
